title: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC): How to Fill It In for Free
summary: Every foreigner entering Thailand must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online in the 3 days before arrival. It replaced the paper TM6 card on 1 May 2025. It is free on the official site, tdac.immigration.go.th. Sites that charge you are not the government.
seoTitle: TDAC Thailand: Free Digital Arrival Card, 3-Day Rule and Scam Sites
seoDescription: Who needs the Thailand Digital Arrival Card, when to submit it, the only official site (tdac.immigration.go.th) and how to avoid paid copycat sites.

sections.heading: What the TDAC is
paragraphs: The TDAC is an online arrival form run by Thailand's Immigration Bureau with the Ministry of Public Health. It replaced the paper TM6 arrival card from 1 May 2025.
It is not a visa. It only records who you are, how you arrive and where you will stay. You still need the right visa or visa exemption to enter.

sections.heading: Who needs it
paragraphs: All foreigners entering Thailand need a TDAC, whether you arrive by air, land or sea. That includes holders of long-stay visas and extensions.
list: Not needed: transit or transfer passengers who don't pass through Thai immigration control.
Not needed: people entering with a Border Pass.

sections.heading: When to submit it
paragraphs: Submit it in the 3 days before your arrival date. If you submit too early, the system won't accept it. Submitting a day or two before you fly is easiest.
If your plans change, you can edit your TDAC on the official site before you arrive.

sections.heading: How to fill it in
list: Go to tdac.immigration.go.th. Check the address carefully: it ends in .go.th.
Enter your passport details exactly as printed, in English.
Add your flight or vehicle number, arrival date and where you boarded.
Give your first address in Thailand, such as your hotel.
Complete the short health declaration about countries you visited recently.
Submit, then save or screenshot the confirmation with its QR code and number. Immigration may ask to see it.

sections.heading: Watch out for scam sites
paragraphs: Many websites and paid search ads copy the look of the official site and charge a fee, sometimes calling it "urgent" or "express" processing. The official TDAC is free. There is no paid fast track.
Before you type any details, check that the address is exactly tdac.immigration.go.th. If a site asks for a card payment, close it.
list: Free: tdac.immigration.go.th, the only official site.
Red flag: any fee, "service charge" or "urgent processing".
Red flag: a domain that doesn't end in .go.th.
Red flag: no clear company name or address on the site.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
paragraphs: If you forgot to submit, you can usually still do it on your phone before you reach passport control. Keep your passport, flight details and first address ready.
If you already paid a copycat site, contact your card issuer about a refund. Then check you have a real TDAC number from the official site.

No. It is only an arrival card. You still need a visa or visa exemption.

faqs.q: I live in Thailand. Do I still need it?
faqs.a: The official notice says all foreigners need to submit it, so fill it in each time you return, even with a long-stay visa and re-entry permit.

faqs.q: Do children need their own TDAC?
faqs.a: Yes. Every traveller needs one. The official site lets you add fellow travellers in one group submission.

faqs.q: I'm only changing planes in Bangkok. Do I need one?
faqs.a: Not if you stay airside and don't pass through Thai immigration.
